description: Karplus-Strong plucked-string loop, one sample per accepted beat: y(n) = (1 - 2^-E) * (y(n-1) + y(n-M)) / 2 + x(n). a is the s12 excitation sample, c[1:0] selects the loop length M = 4/8/12/16 cells (pitch fs/M at fs = 8000 Hz), c[2] selects the damping exponent E = 4 or 7, c[31] starts a new pluck by clearing the 16-cell line, the pointer and the previous output (that beat rings from silence, its two-tap sum is forced to zero), and c[30:3] must be zero. result is the s12 clamped new cell value, sign extended. aux[3:0] = next pointer, aux[5:4] = M selector, aux[6] = output clamp, aux[7] = restart echo, aux[21:8] = the pre-clamp feedback value. fault = output clamped or malformed control.
hardware_advantage: A plucked-string voice normally wants a delay line in block RAM plus a multiply for the loop gain; here the 16x12 line is a case-mapped register file and the damping is a self-subtracted shifted copy, so a whole tone generator runs at II=1 with no BRAM, no DSP slice and no address multiply, leaving the memory blocks for everything else.
provenance: original source authored in this workspace; no third-party RTL imported
qualification: engineering candidate; not certified production or side-channel protection
